clue.text: One's going round? China may be arrived at soon!

definitions.text: One's going round? China may be arrived at soon!

parts.words: One's going round? China may be arrived at soon!
parts.note: a revolving device on which clay is shaped, so that crockery (china) will soon result from its turning

explanation.surface: Someone travelling round the world expects to reach China shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country on a round-the-world trip, but it is porcelain, and the thing going round is the turntable a craftsman throws clay on.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning disc a ceramicist uses is the thing that turns and from which crockery comes.

clue.text: Jimmy carter, say, as a fellow on the level

definitions.meaning: US president Jimmy Carter comes from the town of Plains, Georgia, so he is a man of Plains
someone who lives on flat grassland prairie

explanation.surface: A former US president is described as an honest, straightforward chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jimmy carter' with a small c pretends to be a man who carts things; the setter means the president from Plains, Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Carter's hometown is Plains, and a dweller of flat open prairie country is also called this.

clue.text: Child, a learner to be given sum

parts.note: a tot is a small child
L is the learner-driver abbreviation, from L-plates

explanation.surface: A child doing a driving course gets set an arithmetic problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the whole amount added up, the overall figure.

clue.text: Discharge source of pollution into river and lake

indicators.note: into means the first letter of pollution goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: source of picks the opening letter of the word pollution

explanation.surface: A factory discharges pollution into a river and a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' reads as a polluting outflow, but it means to throw out; the river is the Exe in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge someone is to dismiss or eject them, as a school throws out a pupil.

clue.text: A ration, as distributed in certain hospitals

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread out and dealt again in a new order

explanation.surface: A food ration is handed out in some hospitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges the nine letters of A RATION AS.
explanation.definitionFit: These were institutions for convalescents or patients with chronic illness such as tuberculosis.

clue.text: Explosive leading article, surprisingly unorthodox

indicators.note: leading means the explosive goes at the front, before the rest

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the word article is rearranged in an unexpected way

explanation.surface: An inflammatory newspaper editorial turns out to be unexpectedly radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading article' looks like a newspaper editorial; 'leading' puts HE first and 'surprisingly' turns ARTICLE into RETICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding beliefs contrary to accepted doctrine is departing from orthodoxy.

clue.text: Temptress not avoiding love affair

parts.note: Eve tempted Adam with the apple in Genesis

indicators.note: avoiding means the word not goes without the letter for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A seductress is not shying away from a romantic liaison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' reads as romance in the surface but means an occasion; 'avoiding' strips O from NOT to leave NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean any happening or occasion, such as a social function.

clue.text: Vagrants hoping the tide will turn in their favour?

definitions.text: Vagrants hoping the tide will turn in their favour?

parts.words: Vagrants hoping the tide will turn in their favour?
parts.note: drifters who scour the shoreline hope the sea will wash up something useful for them

explanation.surface: Down-and-outs hope their luck is about to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tide will turn' is the idiom for luck changing, but here it is literal: the sea washing up items on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Shore scavengers search sand and shingle for things the sea has left behind.

clue.text: Praise old flame a lot though lacking love

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: lacking means the phrase a lot goes without the letter for love

parts.note: a lot written as one run of letters
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone praises a former partner a great deal, despite no longer loving them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking love' takes O out of A LOT, leaving ALT.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify or extol someone is to praise them highly.

clue.text: Writer out of immediate touch with his reader?

definitions.text: Writer out of immediate touch with his reader?

parts.words: Writer out of immediate touch with his reader?
parts.note: someone who corresponds by letter with a distant person they may never have met

explanation.surface: An author has lost contact with his audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' and 'reader' suggest an author and his public; here they are two people exchanging letters across the miles.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent known only through letters is far away from the person who reads them.

clue.text: Girl with something to tell? Writes article in that medical book

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

indicators.note: in means the writing and the article are put inside the tale

parts.note: a story is something to tell
pens means writes
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl with gossip to share writes a piece in a medical journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PENS and A inside STORY, giving S-PENSA-TORY after DI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old word for a pharmacopoeia, a reference work listing medicines and how to prepare them.

clue.text: Like meal with lover that's wicked!

definitions.text: Like meal with lover that's wicked!

parts.words: Like meal with lover that's wicked!
parts.note: a romantic dinner is lit by tapers, and wicked here means having a wick

explanation.surface: A dinner with an illicit partner is shockingly sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' suggests sin with a lover, but it means fitted with wicks, as tapers on a romantic dinner table are.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic dinner is typically illuminated by tapers, which have wicks.

clue.text: Bird at the front of American book

indicators.note: at the front of puts the bird before the American abbreviation

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird is pictured on the front of an American book cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is the New Testament letter to Titus.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the epistles of the New Testament, so a part of the Bible.

clue.text: Firm male, chap facing the German officer

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a chap is a man
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A company's male employee stands up to a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' just joins the pieces; 'Firm' looks like an adjective but is the noun, a company.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a military or naval rank of officer, such as one who leads a ship.

clue.text: Agreeing the bill's binding

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, the bill
cording is cord used to tie or bind

explanation.surface: Both sides agree that the bill is legally binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' looks like legally enforceable, but it is cord for tying things.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in accord or harmony with something means consenting or matching it.

clue.text: Want of respect is seen on estate when judge goes around

indicators.note: goes around means the verb for judge wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to deem is to judge or consider
est. is an abbreviation for estate

explanation.surface: A landowner shows disrespect when a judge tours the property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes around' puts IS and EST inside DEEM, after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old word for lack of regard or low opinion, the opposite of high regard.

clue.text: Taxi left before end of dance — one's stranded

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word dance

explanation.surface: Someone takes a cab home before the dance ends, leaving a partner stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's stranded' suggests being left high and dry; it means made of strands, like a rope or wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick rope or wire is made of twisted strands.

clue.text: Legal expert upset gentleman in deal

indicators.note: in means the upturned title goes inside the trade word

parts.note: to barter is to deal or trade

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word sir is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knighted gentleman

explanation.surface: A lawyer is upset that a gentleman was involved in the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks emotional; it reverses SIR to RIS, and 'in' puts it inside BARTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtroom lawyer in England, one entitled to plead in the higher courts.

clue.text: Frenzied Scot goes round province

indicators.note: goes round means the Scottish name encircles the province

parts.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scotsman
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A Scotsman travels round a region in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'province' is Northern Ireland, often called the Province in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildly excited and overactive, as in a mood of high frenzy.

clue.text: Some unable to reach holster to get guns?

definitions.text: Some unable to reach holster to get guns?

parts.words: Some unable to reach holster to get guns?
parts.note: people with short limbs would not reach the hip, and the phrase also names light firearms

explanation.surface: Some gunmen cannot reach their holsters to draw their weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Short limbs would fail to reach a holster; the same phrase names light handheld firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and rifles, weapons carried by hand, are known by this phrase.

clue.text: Come into American HQ avoiding the front entrance

indicators.note: avoiding the front entrance means the word drops its first letter, the way in

parts.note: center is the American spelling of centre, a headquarters

explanation.surface: Visitors arrive at the American headquarters by a back door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding the front entrance' drops C, the first letter, from CENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To go inside a place is to step in or gain entry.

clue.text: Tease the 'unmanned' female of the family

indicators.note: unmanned means the word the loses the pronoun for a man

parts.note: an aunt is a female relative

explanation.surface: A family's female member is mocked for losing her nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unmanned' removes HE, a man, from THE, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke or mock someone with jibes is to tease them.

clue.text: See mean person hide somewhere in north Wales

parts.note: skin is a hide
Flint is a town in north-east Wales

explanation.surface: Look out for a miser hiding somewhere in north Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link; 'hide' is a noun, an animal's skin. Flint is a town in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser who hates parting with money is stingy.

clue.text: Playwright making money after one book

indicators.note: after means the money comes later, behind the other two pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: A dramatist starts earning after his first book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts SEN, a Japanese coin, behind I and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House.

clue.text: Discarded female, a 'windbag'

parts.note: a lung is literally a bag holding air

explanation.surface: A woman who talks too much gets dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windbag' suggests a chatterbox, but is the literal air sack in the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown away or cast aside has been hurled off.

clue.text: Ribaldry causes sin unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately signals the letters fall out badly into a new order

explanation.surface: Bawdy humour regrettably leads to sinful behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges CAUSES SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky, risque or bawdy humour is cheekiness of a naughty kind.

clue.text: Golf club without leader, say

indicators.note: without leader means the club name loses its first letter

parts.note: a putter is a golf club for the green

explanation.surface: A golfer speaks about a club with no captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf club' looks like a members' club lacking a leader; it is the putter, losing P.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak or voice words is to say them.

clue.text: One responsible for technical crew — men at garages possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: The man in charge of mechanics turns out to be a garage foreman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MEN AT GARAGES; the crew is a theatre's backstage crew, not mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, this person runs the backstage team and the performance's cues.
